LESSON: MILAD UN-NABI

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Milad un-Nabi

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Milad un-Nabi. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: When was the Prophet 7. 0 ISLAMIC learner should be able to: praise of the Prophet (S.A.W). (S.A.W) born?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MILAD UN-NABI
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Milad un-Nabi helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MILAD UN-NABI
Study Milad un-Nabi like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children

What this means
In this part you learn to Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Milad un-Nabi” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Milad un-Nabi is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Milad un-Nabi” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Milad un-Nabi to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Milad un-Nabi from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Milad un-Nabi: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Milad un-Nabi?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When was the Prophet 7. 0 ISLAMIC learner should be able to: praise of the Prophet (S.A.W). (S.A.W) born?
2. when a place during Aqiqah ceremony Aqiqah ceremony. baby is born?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Milad un-Nabi means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Appreciate Aqiqah as an Islamic ritual for all children.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
